answer: A Sybil-resistant check could use a tidal inlet watch tied to a spiral gauge. Each applicant gets one small inlet with a spiral-marked tide staff, and must log water height and an ivory marker buoy's position at times announced only hours ahead. Tides and drift differ by inlet, so a scripted farm cannot fabricate convincing series in advance. One person cannot attend many distant inlets at short notice. Neighbouring watchers cross-check logs against their own gauges, so many fake identities would need many real coastal observers, while an honest participant watches one nearby inlet.
